instruction: Use ANSYS Mechanical APDL to build and solve an axisymmetric circular plate model. For this task, open Mechanical APDL from `C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe`. Physical problem: A thin circular plate with a clamped outer edge is subjected to a uniform transverse pressure. Coordinate system and geometry: - Use a 2D axisymmetric model with PLANE183. - In the axisymmetric cross-section, X is the radial direction and Y is the axial/thickness direction. - The symmetry axis is X = 0. - Model the rectangular cross-section 0 <= X <= 50 mm and 0 <= Y <= 1 mm. - The clamped outer edge is X = 50 mm. - The loaded top surface is Y = 1 mm. Model parameters: - Material: linear elastic steel. - Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa. - Poisson's ratio = 0.3. - Enable the PLANE183 axisymmetric option. Mesh: - Use a mapped quadrilateral mesh. - Use 25 uniform element divisions in the radial X direction. - Use 4 uniform element divisions through the thickness in the Y direction. - The final mesh must contain 100 PLANE183 elements. Boundary conditions and load: - On the symmetry axis X = 0, set UX = 0. - On the clamped outer edge X = 50 mm, set UX = 0 and UY = 0. - Apply a uniform pressure of 0.1 MPa on Y = 1 mm, acting in the negative Y direction. Analysis type: - Static structural analysis. Save requirements: - Use C:\Users\user\Desktop as the ANSYS working directory. - Save the database file as C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_plate.db. - Save the structural result file as C:\Users\user\Desktop\apdl_plate.rst. - Run the solver to completion and save the final solved state in both files.

command: $licenseOutput = & python 'C:\Users\user\Desktop\license.py' 2>&1; $licenseCode = $LASTEXITCODE; $licenseText = $licenseOutput | Out-String; if ($licenseCode -ne 0 -or -not $licenseText.Contains('[SUCCESS]')) { exit 1 }; Start-Process -FilePath 'C:\Program Files\ANSYS Inc\v261\ansys\bin\winx64\ANSYS261.exe' -ArgumentList '-g'
